summary: Optimizing LLM usage at inference time can cut API spend by 50-90% while simultaneously reducing latency, often turning a $10K monthly bill into $2K or less. The highest-leverage techniques — prompt caching, semantic caching, and model cascading — require minimal engineering effort and deliver immediate returns. Combining several techniques compounds savings, with production teams routinely achieving 60-80% cost reductions without sacrificing output quality.

techniques.name: Prompt Caching
techniques.description: Reuse cached portions of repeated input prompts (system prompts, few-shot examples, long context) so providers only charge a fraction of the input token cost for the cached prefix. This is the highest-leverage, lowest-risk optimization for production teams in 2026.
techniques.savings: up to 90% reduction on input costs for repeated prompts
techniques.example: Place a large static system prompt and document context at the start of every request so Anthropic's cache_control marks it cacheable, reducing repeat-call input cost to ~10% of the original.

techniques.name: Semantic Caching
techniques.description: Store previous query/response pairs as embeddings and return a cached answer when a new query is semantically similar (not just an exact match), avoiding a redundant LLM call entirely. Production hit rates of ~68% are achievable.
techniques.example: Use GPTCache or a Redis semantic cache so that 'What's your refund policy?' and 'How do I get a refund?' both resolve to one cached answer instead of two API calls.

techniques.name: Model Cascading / Routing
techniques.description: Route simple requests to small, cheap models and escalate only hard queries to expensive frontier models, optionally using a cheap classifier to decide. Most queries never need the top-tier model.
techniques.example: Send all queries to GPT-4o-mini first and only fall back to GPT-4o when the cheaper model's confidence or a validation check fails.

techniques.name: Prompt Compression / Optimization
techniques.description: Trim verbose instructions, remove redundant few-shot examples, and compress context (e.g. with LLMLingua) to reduce input tokens while preserving meaning.
techniques.example: Replace a 500-token rambling system prompt with a tightly-worded 150-token version, or run LLMLingua to compress retrieved documents before sending them.

techniques.name: Output Token Limiting
techniques.description: Cap response length with max_tokens and instruct the model to be concise or return structured/JSON output, since output tokens are typically billed 2-4x more than input tokens.
techniques.example: Set max_tokens=200 and add 'Respond in under 3 sentences' to stop the model from generating long, expensive, unnecessary prose.

techniques.name: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) over long context
techniques.description: Instead of stuffing entire documents into the prompt, retrieve only the most relevant chunks via vector search, drastically cutting input token volume.
techniques.example: Retrieve the top 3 relevant passages from a vector store and inject only those 1,500 tokens instead of pasting a 40,000-token manual into every call.

techniques.name: Batching Requests
techniques.description: Group multiple requests into a single API call or use provider batch endpoints that offer ~50% discounts for asynchronous processing.
techniques.savings: up to 50% reduction via batch pricing
techniques.example: Submit 10,000 non-urgent classification jobs through OpenAI's Batch API overnight to pay half the synchronous rate.

techniques.name: Right-Sizing the Model
techniques.description: Choose the smallest model that meets quality requirements rather than defaulting to the flagship, evaluating cheaper or open-source models for each task.
techniques.example: Switch a summarization feature from GPT-4o to GPT-4o-mini or Llama 3.1 8B after confirming output quality is acceptable on your eval set.

techniques.name: Streaming and Early Termination
techniques.description: Stream responses and stop generation as soon as the needed content (e.g. a parseable field) is produced, avoiding paying for trailing tokens.
techniques.example: Stream a JSON response and abort the connection once the closing brace of the required object is received.

tools.name: GPTCache
tools.description: Open-source semantic cache for LLM queries that stores embeddings and returns cached responses for similar prompts, reducing API calls.
tools.pricing_paid: Free (open source); self-hosting infra costs only

tools.name: Redis (Semantic Cache / LangCache)
tools.description: Vector-enabled Redis used as a high-performance semantic cache layer for LLM responses, matching queries by meaning to avoid redundant calls.
tools.pricing_paid: Free open-source Redis; Redis Cloud from ~$5/mo, enterprise tiers available

tools.name: LiteLLM
tools.description: Unified proxy/SDK across 100+ LLM providers with built-in caching, routing, fallback, and cost tracking for easy model cascading.
tools.pricing_paid: Free open source; Enterprise plans with SSO/support (custom pricing)

tools.name: Helicone
tools.description: LLM observability and gateway platform offering caching, cost monitoring, rate limiting, and prompt analytics.
tools.pricing_paid: Free tier (10k requests/mo); paid plans from ~$20/mo

tools.name: LangChain
tools.description: Framework for building LLM apps with built-in LLM response caching (in-memory, Redis, SQLite), RAG pipelines, and routing abstractions.
tools.pricing_paid: Free open source; LangSmith observability from ~$39/user/mo

tools.name: LLMLingua
tools.description: Microsoft prompt-compression tool that reduces prompt length up to 20x while preserving key information, cutting input token costs.

tools.name: Portkey
tools.description: AI gateway with semantic caching, smart routing, load balancing, fallbacks, and cost/usage observability across providers.

tools.name: OpenRouter
tools.description: Unified API aggregating many model providers with automatic routing and price comparison to pick the cheapest suitable model.
tools.pricing_paid: Pay-per-use at underlying model prices plus small routing fee

quick_wins: Enable prompt caching on your provider (Anthropic cache_control / OpenAI automatic caching) to slash input costs on repeated system prompts by up to 90%.
Switch default traffic from a flagship model to a cheaper small model (e.g. GPT-4o-mini) and only escalate when quality checks fail.
Set sensible max_tokens limits and instruct the model to be concise to cut expensive output token spend.
Add a semantic cache (GPTCache or Redis) in front of your LLM calls to eliminate redundant requests, targeting ~68% hit rates.
Trim and compress your prompts — remove redundant instructions and few-shot examples — for an immediate 20-60% input token reduction.
